title: The Dog Night, 2020
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: Twenty-one years. The last one in the public strip. The bulb is out again. Nobody replaces it this time.

panels.composition: Behind the Lanes. The bulb dark. The bin. The outline, fading. WOOD and BARNABY II lit only by the sign's few remaining letters.

image.prompt: a man and a three-legged dog behind a bowling alley at night, the bulb dark, a blue bin, a fading rust outline on the gravel, lit only by the faint pink of a mostly-dead neon sign, clean ink with one tone, no words

panels.composition: The pup, six, sitting. The outline barely there under him.

image.prompt: close-up of a three-legged dog sitting on gravel where a rust outline has almost faded away, no words

panels.composition: The porch. The box has finally collapsed; it's flat. The pup lying on the flat cardboard anyway. Wood on the step.

image.prompt: a three-legged dog lying on a completely flattened weathered produce box on a porch, a man on the step, night, no words

panels.composition: The sign. Eight dark. The rest flicker. Wood looking. This is the last Dog Night the public strip draws.

image.prompt: a man on a porch looking at a distant bowling-alley sign with eight letters dark and the remainder flickering, a dog on a flattened box beside him, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet; 2019: the Sunday drawn to a smaller grid
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust; 2020: ochre and slate arriving

notes: The last public Dog Night. Bulb out for good. The box flat. Eight dark.
